item.title: FPL Mobilizes 5,000 Crews Across 29 States to Restore Power to 332,000 Panhandle Customers

item.content:encoded:
Florida Power & Light has deployed crews from across the nation to restore electricity to more than 332,000 customers in the Panhandle following what appears to be a significant weather event. The utility has mobilized approximately 5,000 restoration workers from 29 states to accelerate recovery efforts in the region.

The scale of the outage and multi-state response suggests a major weather system impacted the area. Escambia County residents and businesses across the Panhandle remain without power as crews work to repair infrastructure and reconnect service.

FPL has not yet provided an estimated timeline for full restoration, though the company's mobilization of such a large workforce indicates the utility is treating the situation with urgency. Customers experiencing outages are advised to check FPL's website or contact the utility for updates on service restoration in their specific areas.

item.title: Santa Rosa Sheriff warns of scammers targeting Hurricane Isaias victims
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office is alerting residents to be on guard against fraudsters attempting to exploit people affected by Hurricane Isaias. Scammers often target disaster victims by posing as contractors, insurance adjusters, or relief workers seeking payment for cleanup, repairs, or assistance. Residents should verify the legitimacy…
item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office is alerting residents to be on guard against fraudsters attempting to exploit people affected by Hurricane Isaias.

Scammers often target disaster victims by posing as contractors, insurance adjusters, or relief workers seeking payment for cleanup, repairs, or assistance. Residents should verify the legitimacy of anyone requesting money or personal information before providing either.

The Sheriff's Office advises victims to work only with licensed contractors, check credentials carefully, and report suspicious activity to local law enforcement. More details on common hurricane-related scams and how to protect yourself are available through the Sheriff's Office.

item.title: DOH-Santa Rosa Reopening Limited Services Wednesday After Weather
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will partially reopen Wednesday following severe weather that forced closures, according to a statement from the health department's public information office. Only two offices will resume operations with limited hours: the Women, Infant, and Children (WIC) office will be open from 7:30 a.m. to…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will partially reopen Wednesday following severe weather that forced closures, according to a statement from the health department's public information office.

Only two offices will resume operations with limited hours: the Women, Infant, and Children (WIC) office will be open from 7:30 a.m. to noon, and the Vital Statistics office will operate from 8 a.m. to noon, both in Milton.

The health department says hours and services for Thursday and Friday will be announced in a separate update. Residents needing more information can call DOH-Santa Rosa at 850-983-5200.

item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will resume limited operations this week following severe weather that forced closures. Beginning Wednesday, October 14, only the Women, Infant, and Children (WIC) office and Vital Statistics office in Milton will be open.

The WIC office will operate from 7:30 a.m. to noon, while Vital Statistics will be available from 8 a.m. to noon on Wednesday. The health department said it will release updated hours and service information for Thursday and Friday in a separate announcement.

Residents needing to reach the department can call 850-983-5200 for more details. The partial reopening represents the first step toward full restoration of services at the Santa Rosa County health offices.

item.title: Pensacola Day 4: Power restored to 97K as cleanup continues
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As Pensacola enters its fourth day of recovery from Hurricane Isaias, city crews are maintaining round-the-clock efforts to clear debris and restore critical services, according to an 11 a.m. update from the City of Pensacola Public Information Office. Florida Power & Light has restored electricity to approximately 97,000 customers across Escambia…
item.content:encoded:
As Pensacola enters its fourth day of recovery from Hurricane Isaias, city crews are maintaining round-the-clock efforts to clear debris and restore critical services, according to an 11 a.m. update from the City of Pensacola Public Information Office.

Florida Power & Light has restored electricity to approximately 97,000 customers across Escambia County as of Monday morning. City officials are urging residents to remain cautious as downed trees, power lines, and other storm hazards remain scattered throughout the area.

"Our crews have been working nonstop, pitching in wherever they are needed," the city said in its update. "They're tired. You're tired. But remember this is a marathon, not a sprint." The focus remains on public safety, debris removal, and restoring critical infrastructure and services to the community.

item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias caused significant damage to Santa Rosa Christian School's Learning Center in Santa Rosa County, with the storm ripping the roof off the facility, according to WKRG News 5.

The damage has created major operational challenges for the school as it assesses the full extent of the destruction and begins recovery efforts. The Learning Center, a key part of the school's infrastructure, will require substantial repairs before it can resume normal operations.

The storm's impact on Santa Rosa County schools underscores the region's vulnerability to major hurricanes and highlights the need for continued preparedness and resilience planning among local institutions.

item.title: Taddeo Campaign Launches Ad Attacking Ingoglia's CFO Record
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democrat Annette Taddeo's campaign for Florida Chief Financial Officer rolled out a new digital ad Monday attacking Republican Blaise Ingoglia's tenure in the office, according to a press release from CVS Communications. The 30-second spot highlights recent scrutiny of the Department of Financial Services under Ingoglia's watch, including missing…
item.content:encoded:
Democrat Annette Taddeo's campaign for Florida Chief Financial Officer rolled out a new digital ad Monday attacking Republican Blaise Ingoglia's tenure in the office, according to a press release from CVS Communications. The 30-second spot highlights recent scrutiny of the Department of Financial Services under Ingoglia's watch, including missing documentation for more than $342 million in contracts and a grand jury's findings on a $10 million Hope Florida Medicaid settlement.

The ad accuses Ingoglia of giving insurance companies a $3 billion bailout and diverting $10 million meant for sick children toward political activity. "Ingoglia's corruption has gone wild, and it's costing you more," the narrator states, before Taddeo pledges to lower insurance rates and ensure accountability.

Taddeo, a South Florida business owner who founded LanguageSpeak three decades ago, flipped a Republican state Senate seat in 2017 to become the first Latina Democrat elected to the Florida Senate. She served five years on the Banking and Insurance Committee before launching her bid for the statewide financial oversight position, focusing on insurance costs, accountability, and protecting taxpayer dollars.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College announced Monday that all its locations will remain closed Tuesday, October 13, as the college continues to assess conditions before resuming operations.

The closure affects all classes, campus activities, special events, and online instruction. The college is still evaluating when it will be safe to reopen and has not yet announced a firm date for resuming normal operations.

Fall B session final exams and the start of the D session will be rescheduled once PSC determines when classes can resume. Students and staff are urged to monitor PSC's social media accounts, the college website at PensacolaState.edu, and PSC Alert for updates as the situation develops.

item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa Island Authority has canceled its committee meeting scheduled for Wednesday, October 14, according to a news release from the agency.

All items that were set for discussion during the committee meeting will instead be addressed at the SRIA's next full board meeting, scheduled for Wednesday, October 28. The authority, which oversees operations on Pensacola Beach, did not provide a reason for the cancellation.

Residents and those interested in SRIA business can find updated meeting information at sria-fla.com. The Santa Rosa Island Authority operates under the direction of Escambia County and receives its funding entirely from lease fees paid by businesses and residents on Pensacola Beach.

item.title: Escambia County Schools Closed Tuesday for Storm Damage Repairs
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Public Schools will remain closed Tuesday, October 13, as the district works to repair damage and restore essential services across its campuses, according to a Monday announcement from ECPS Communications. School officials say district personnel and contractors are actively addressing damage from what appears to be recent severe…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Public Schools will remain closed Tuesday, October 13, as the district works to repair damage and restore essential services across its campuses, according to a Monday announcement from ECPS Communications.

School officials say district personnel and contractors are actively addressing damage from what appears to be recent severe weather. The district is coordinating with local utility companies to restore power and other vital services to school buildings. Transportation teams are also assessing bus routes to ensure safe operations before resuming service.

"The safety of our students, their families, our employees and this community remains our top priority," the district said in a statement. ECPS said it will post further updates through its Focus Communications system, social media, and local media outlets as repairs continue.

item.title: ECMS Foundation Names 16 Finalists for 3rd Annual Health Excellence Awards
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Medical Society Foundation has announced the finalists for its third consecutive year of Health Excellence Awards, recognizing individuals and organizations improving health outcomes in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties. Sixteen finalists were selected from nominations submitted by colleagues, patients, and community members.…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Medical Society Foundation has announced the finalists for its third consecutive year of Health Excellence Awards, recognizing individuals and organizations improving health outcomes in Escambia and Santa Rosa Counties.

Sixteen finalists were selected from nominations submitted by colleagues, patients, and community members. The winner announcement will take place Thursday, October 29 at 6:00 p.m. at the Jean & Paul Amos Performance Studio. According to the foundation, awards will be presented across seven categories that include both clinical and non-clinical roles, as well as honors for ECMS Physician Members.

"Every one of these finalists was nominated by someone who sees their work up close and wanted to make sure it was recognized," said Ellen W. McKnight, MD, president of the ECMS Foundation. The finalists represent a range of healthcare professionals and supporters working in the local medical community.

Tickets and sponsorships for the October 29 event are available at escambiacms.org/hea. The foundation notes that past years have sold out, and encourages early registration. Emerald Coast Hospice is returning as the Legacy Presenting Sponsor. Proceeds benefit the ECMS Foundation's community health programs, which include the Go Seniors! Transportation program, the Blood Pressure Cuff Program, and physician wellness initiatives, along with scholarships at FSU College of Medicine's Pensacola Regional Campus and Pensacola State College.

item.title: Sunny, warm stretch expected this week across NW Florida

item.content:encoded: Expect pleasant weather over the next several days across the Pensacola area and North Escambia County. Monday through Wednesday will feature consistent sunshine with highs hovering near 87 degrees and calm winds, according to the National Weather Service forecast. Overnight lows will dip to around 61–62 degrees under clear skies. No rain is expected through at least midweek, making it an ideal stretch for outdoor activities.
